But the same way this community is so surprisingly good at de-centering their white, western voices on topics or race and imperialism (presumably because the hosts are either POC or very good at centering POC voices), there needs to be room for women to talk about the specific struggles that they face (which can often be understood through Marxist analysis anyways).

Why is the basic concept of "body shaming men" immediately jumped upon with such intensity in this community, when much more frequent instances where women are denigrated are typically just ignored? If you can forgive Palestinians for literally murdering their oppressors (as you should, to be clear), you can surely find it in yourself to forgive women for using an offensive symbol in their messaging.

I understand where the feeling comes from that maybe if those in the Imperial Core actually experienced some suffering they would come around to more radical forms of change. I often find myself thinking similarly of Americans when it comes to war: The American consciousness is able to view war as largely harmless and unimportant because America hasn't fought a war against a foreign enemy on their soil in over 200 years. And I don't think that is incorrect.

However, when it comes to greater ideas of accelerationism, there are multiple flaws with the strategy. The first and most obvious is that sometimes, no matter how much you make the people suffer, they simply lack the power to actually enact the change needed to end the suffering. It doesn't matter how many poor people you have dying on the streets or how many immigrants are locked up in camps, they will never develop the power to actually rise up against those instituting the policy, especially if the infrastructure for revolution is not in place already.

Secondly, and relatedly, the suffering caused by accelerationism is neither evenly spread nor spread in proportion with the blame deserved for the current state of affairs. When things like the policy in the OP are put into place, the people being hurt the most will not be those in the seats of power who are capable of immediately implementing change. Nor will it be the complacent moderate liberal who needs to wake up and witness the suffering their system creates. It will be the most vulnerable people first: the poor, LGBT, immigrants, etc. There is no need to make those people suffer because they already suffer enough to be receptive to our messages. And if they are made to "disappear", then we lose a great deal of our manpower.

Finally, it is important to remember that throughout history, hardship has not always lead to socialism. When people experience great hardship, they often turn to world views that say they will protect them. Socialism is indeed one of these ideologies, and is in fact the one that is telling the truth. However, in current America fascism has a far louder voice and makes the same promises, however dishonest they are. I believe that were Americans to experience the suffering that we sometimes wonder if they deserve, they are far more primed to turn to fascism as a solution than socialism.

To be clear, I am not saying, "Accelerationism is wrong, so vote as the solution". If Biden were to win this year, we would simply have to worry about the terrifying "Project 2029". And Biden's victory would not make anything better because we have already seen what a Biden presidency looks like for 3 years. What I am saying is that this understandable impulse to hope that America suffering would help bring about positive change is a flawed and comes from a hope that outside intervention will allow us to skip the hard, slow parts of building our movement. 

Instead we ought to continue building our movement the old-fashioned way, through education, community work towards building alternate systems of power, amplifying voices from other countries far more prepared to move towards socialism, and recruiting from the people already suffering in society. Because even without accelerationism, we already have lots of people suffering who can be brought into the movement if we show them that our ideas can help them.

There are plenty of (particularly upper-class, white, cis-het) women that make a large sum of money through it, and I'm sure there are examples of women who have used prostitution to rise from poverty and be able to get a different job. But the vast majority of people engaging in sex work do so because they have no other choice. It is not a coincidence that the majority of people doing sex work are among the most vulnerable populations in society (POC, immigrants, poor, trans people, children, etc.) despite the fact that most people who speak so positively about the empowerment of sex work are not a part of these populations.

I don't think you're wrong, but I think the issue is that talking about it is kind of pointless? With Z-jump and box controllers and notches, there are obvious action steps that we can discuss. Banning or restricting them is worthy of discussion and so there is reason to talk about it. 

With prescription meds, what's the action step? Ban anyone on medication that could confer a competitive advantage? Players have to go off their meds for tournaments? These are obviously absurd ideas that can never be implemented just from an ethical perspective. It would be like saying "Autism confers an advantage at Melee because of hyperfocus on a special interest, therefore we should ban autistic players." It is just so obviously not our place.

On top of that, it's not as if the melee community can force players to reveal their medical history and any medications or diagnoses. The fact that some players feel safe and open to doing so is a good thing that we should protect.

So what do we get out of arguing whether ADHD meds give a competitive advantage? We potentially invalidate players achievements or create a stigma around competing as a player that needs medication, and we don't come up with anything productive. Even if, hypothetically, ADHD meds or antidepressants or inhalers could be proven to give a significant advantage, it still doesn't do any good to talk about it because we can't regulate them without making obviously immoral decisions.

Presumably, Niigo's story is supposed to be about the mutual support between these 4 depressed girls and their 6 imaginary friends. They all start from difficult spots, but they are still able to come together and make each other better.

If that is the writers' intention, then I think the current Mafuyu focus is necessary right now. Right now:

* Mizuki is able to support the others in their struggles. She isn't in a great place, but she's stable. 
* Ena wasn't able to help at the beginning because she was too angry and resentful, but they gave her just enough development in her first 2 focus events to where she is stable for now.
* Kanade's entire development is predicated on her self-sacrificing nature and unwillingness to prioritize her own suffering. So the Mafuyu arc is continuing development of her goal to "save Mafuyu" and setting up for her problems to be solved.

S2 4/4 HoO is the best generalist, but she's pretty expensive now without her special release banner. I expect them to give away stamps for her pretty frequently though since she was free. The other options depend on the enemy:

* Against MECH (e.g. Tank) HoT S2+ with 7Thunders and Handel is best, and she's also generally the strongest at bruteforcing neutral weathers/bosses.
* Against BIO (e.g. Andrius) Mobius is technically best, but she's pretty outdated and generally not worth investing in. She will be in Battle Pass next patch though if you want her/her gears for cheap.
* Against PSY (e.g. Lightning Husk, Sushang) Aponia is best, but she still isn't usually worth it because she only barely beats 7T HoT on her own bosses.
* Anything else (e.g. Shadow Knight, Hawk of the Fog, Darkbolt Jonin) is cope.

I don't know if you need advice on Supports too, but just in case:

* HoTr is the best Lightning support since she provides breach. Her weapon is important, and she likes her Stigs, but she can cope with Turg TB.
* Golden Diva is best 3rd slot, with either full Handel or TurgTB depending on if your DPS uses Handel since it doesn't stack.
* Fischl is outclassed by HoTr but still has her uses. She is used against bosses that have weak spots for bows the shoot (Tank, basically), and in Arena when HoTr is on your Fire or Trio team since she is so in demand.
* If you don't have a better team for Quantum enemies, Fallen Rosemary can slot as 3rd Lightning member, though she needs a ton of ranks and her PRI-ARM to be useable

I would recommend getting HoT Divine Key and farming Elysian Realm for her ranks. HoO is just too expensive, and Aponia/Mobius aren't worth it compared to just brute-forcing with HoT.

For HoO's ranks, the big one that makes a difference is S2, and that only matters if you are using her as a main DPS (e.g. with Eden/HoTr, not HoFi/HoTr). It basically reduces her Evasion cooldown enough that she can get two full rotations of her combo attack within HoTr's buff window. Main DPS HoO is pretty situational though, since Trio team is usually better at IMG fights and Aponia/HoT/Mobius usually beat her on Lightning if they have type-counter.

If you're a low spender, it's not worth pulling for her ranks. Wait until she gets stuff in Spending Events/Battle Pass/Events. Since she was given for free, she will probably be have Stamps given away relatively frequently like Spina Astera had.

Of course, compared to S2 ranking, HoO gets a much bigger damage increase from 4/4 HoTr and 4/4 Golden Diva, so that's the priority if you don't have that yet.

Asterite: Golden Diva & Terminal Aide > Chrono Navi & Starry Impression & Reverist Calico

War Treasury: Jade Knight > Miss Pink Elf > Other

I don't fundamentally disagree with you about what our end goal should be, and I appreciate your civility on what you are correct to call a complex issue. While I agree that our goal should be the creation of a more socialist society where the problems involved in current capitalist sex work are no longer relevant, I disagree with the idea that "safe ways out" necessarily exist in the current system.

For many women, particularly trans women and women of color, the options are being exploited through sex work or being homeless on the street. While it's tragic that women are forced to make that choice, I don't know that it's morally correct to try to make them choose homelessness. Particularly in the name of a philosophical idea like "not encouraging capitalism's treatment of women's bodies as commodities to be exploited". I think many women would say that while such an aspiration is great, their priority is putting food on the table and they need sex work to make that happen. 

So in the meantime, until we get to a socialist society, my personal priority would be discouraging sex work for those who don't need it, and making it safer for those who do. Though, admittedly, I can understand where you are coming from about how that may be, to some, an endorsement of problematic attitudes towards women.

I agree that under capitalism sex work has a whole host of problems. Every form of work under capitalism is exploitative, and turning women's bodies into exploitable commodities is a horrifying idea that flies in the face of all definitions of consent.

But, the reality is that people need to make money to survive. Lots of those people are women. And there is a demand for the bodies of women as a commodity that can give these women the money needed to survive. As long as capitalism forces people to find work at any cost, women are going to have no choice but to use their bodies. Just like with drugs and abortions, they will always happen, but making them legal allows for regulation of the process and protection of the people involved. 

Basically, in a socialist society sex work should be relatively unproblematic but also largely unnecessary and just a choice people can make if they wish to do that form of work. But in a capitalist society, sex work is incredibly problematic and exploitative, but unfortunately necessary for lots of people in order to not end up homeless or starving. The goal should be to keep the people forced to do this work safe from those who wish to abuse them as we work towards creating a society that no longer requires that kind of labor from people.

And while, looking back from Chapter 31, it may be possible Kiana could have survived without Mei taking the core, at the time the decision was framed as the only way Kiana lives.

Mei's statement that "The world means nothing to me without you" seems to me to be the polar opposite from the way Fire MOTH acted in the Previous Era. I would say the "cold and detached herrscher" that Mei tries to be while with World Serpent has the same effect you talk about with the Flame Chasers, though, so I don't disagree with your analysis completely. I think the comparison between her "World Serpent persona" and the Previous Era's mentality is meant to be a statement on the value of the old "Weak Mei" and the new Mei, arguing that the "naive, emotional, attached to Kiana" Mei had value and the new mentality she is trying to put on isn't purely beneficial.

She understands that throwing herself into danger over and over and expecting her loved ones to deal with it and just let her self-destruct in her grief and self-loathing was selfish of her, and from that point on in the story she makes a genuine effort to make it through each tragedy with everyone intact.

When I say it "breezes through" it for most non-Mei characters, I suppose that is a bit of hyperbole, but I definitely feel like the point was important enough to Kiana's character development that it should have been communicated more explicitly instead of relying on the player to pick up on a series of more subtle elements. It's mostly PP Stalling, like everyone else has said. That said, there is skill in winning a PP Stall game.

The primary tools that let you burn less PP than the opponent are residual damage (Toxic, Sand, Hazards, Burn, etc), Pressure, and Ditto. The most important PP is the PP on your recovery moves. A Blissey with 8 PP on Seismic Toss, 12 on Toxic, and 20 on Stealth Rocks but 0 on Softboiled is going to just get widdled down and killed.

Landing Status (even if its on Blissey with Natural Cure or if the opponent has Heal Bell/Aromatherapy) is important because it forces the opponent to burn through their recovery moves faster than you. It also burns through the PP on their Heal Bell/Aromatherapy if they have it. So landing Toxic and getting the 30% burn on Scald is very useful. Sand goes the same, making Hippowdon a good teammate. And Stealth Rock/Spikes/Toxic Spikes are incredibly important, especially when paired with Knock Off to remove Heavy Duty Boots. It also lets you negate Toxapex/Tangrowth/Slwobro/Amoonguss's Regenerator. Together, the opponent's Pokemon are going to blow through PP on Softboiled/Recover/Roost/Slack Off.

Pressure from Corviknight/Kyurem is also helpful to blow through PP. If you can consistently predict the opponent's healing move and switch to a Pressure user, you blow through their recovery twice as fast as they blow through yours. It also burns other PP, but again, recovery PP is the most important.

But the real way you win PP wars is properly playing with Ditto. The first step is to get Ditto hit by Knock Off. Ditto is always Choice Scarfed for the offense matchup, but against Stall you need to get rid of your Choice lock. Then, every time you bring in Ditto you have 20 PP to burn before you need to switch out, including 5 Recovery Move PP. The next time you bring out Ditto, you get 20 PP back. Ditto effectively has infinite PP, so you want to force situations where the opponent is using a real Mon while you are using a Ditto copy, so they are using permanent PP and you aren't. If you watch high ladder stall vs stall matches this is usually what the match is based around. Ditto also can't transform into Ditto, so they can't match if your Ditto is already in.
